q.t: The three angles of any triangle add up to:
q.e: Tear off the three corners and put them together — they make a straight line. (A line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side shows why.)

q.t: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. Find the third (in degrees).
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is:
q.e: All three angles are equal and add to 180°, so each is 180 ÷ 3 = 60°.

q.t: A triangle with one angle of 90° is called:
q.e: It is named after its biggest angle — a right angle.

q.t: Can sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm make a triangle?
o: No, because they are all different
q.e: Any two sides together must be longer than the third, or they cannot reach each other. The two shortest (3 + 4 = 7) beat the longest (5).

q.t: An exterior angle of a triangle equals:
o: The sum of the two interior opposite angles
The sum of all three interior angles
q.e: Exterior + adjacent interior = 180°, and the three interior angles = 180°. So the exterior angle must equal the other two interior angles together.

q.t: An isosceles triangle has:
q.e: Isosceles means ‘equal legs’ — exactly two sides (and the two angles opposite them) are equal.

q.t: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is:
o: The side opposite the right angle
Either side forming the right angle
q.e: It faces the biggest angle (90°), so it is also the longest side.

q.t: Can a triangle have two right angles?
o: Yes, if it is large enough
Only if the third angle is 90°
q.e: 90 + 90 = 180 leaves 0° for the third angle, so there is no third corner.

q.t: A triangle with all three sides of different lengths is:
q.e: Scalene = no equal sides. (It may or may not also be right-angled.)

q.t: The angles of a triangle are x°, 2x° and 3x°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 6x = 180, x = 30. Largest = 3x = 90 — a right-angled triangle.

q.t: An exterior angle of a triangle is 120° and one interior opposite angle is 50°. Find the other interior opposite angle (in degrees).
q.e: Exterior angle = sum of the two interior opposite angles: 120 − 50 = 70.

q.t: The vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 40°. Find each base angle (in degrees).
q.e: The two base angles are equal and share 180 − 40 = 140°, so each is 70°.

q.t: A right-angled triangle has legs 6 cm and 8 cm. Find the hypotenuse (in cm).
q.e: Pythagoras: hypotenuse² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100, so the hypotenuse is 10.

q.t: Can sides of 5 cm, 7 cm and 13 cm make a triangle?
o: No, because they are all odd
q.e: The two shorter sides together (12) are shorter than the third (13), so they cannot meet.

q.t: In a right-angled triangle one acute angle is 35°. Find the other acute angle (in degrees).
q.e: The right angle takes 90°, leaving 90° for the other two: 90 − 35 = 55.

q.t: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one leg 5 cm. Find the other leg (in cm).
q.e: leg² = 13² − 5² = 169 − 25 = 144, so the leg is 12.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
q.e: 9 parts make 180°, one part is 20°, largest = 80°.

q.t: Each base angle of an isosceles triangle is 55°. Find the vertex angle (in degrees).
Find each exterior angle of an equilateral triangle (in degrees).
q.e: Each interior angle is 60°, and exterior + interior = 180°, so the exterior angle is 120° (= 60 + 60, the two opposite angles).

q.t: A 15 m ladder reaches a window 12 m above the ground. How far is the foot of the ladder from the wall (in m)?
q.e: Wall, ground and ladder make a right triangle with the ladder as hypotenuse: 15² − 12² = 225 − 144 = 81, so 9 m.

q.t: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110°. The two interior opposite angles are in the ratio 2 : 3. Find the larger of them (in degrees).
q.e: They add up to the exterior angle: 5 parts = 110, one part = 22, larger = 66.

q.t: Two sides of a triangle are 7 cm and 10 cm. The third side must be:
q.e: It must be less than the sum (17) so the other two can reach, and more than the difference (3) so that it can reach them.

q.t: The angles of a triangle are (x + 10)°, (2x − 20)° and (x + 30)°. Find the largest angle (in degrees).
Is a triangle with sides 9 cm, 40 cm and 41 cm right-angled?
o: No, because the sides are unequal
q.e: 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 41². If the squares of two sides add up to the square of the third, the triangle is right-angled.

q.t: One angle of a triangle is 80° and the other two are equal. Find each of them (in degrees).
q.e: The other two share 100° equally: 50° each.

q.t: A rectangle is 8 cm by 15 cm. Find the length of its diagonal (in cm).
q.e: The diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 8 and 15: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17².

q.t: In a triangle, one angle equals the sum of the other two. The triangle is:
q.e: If A = B + C, then A + A = 180, so A = 90°.

q.t: A right-angled triangle is also isosceles. Find each acute angle (in degrees).
q.e: The two acute angles are equal and add to 90°, so each is 45°.

q.t: A man walks 12 m east and then 5 m north. How far is he from his starting point (in m)?
q.e: East and north are at right angles, so the straight-line distance is a hypotenuse: 144 + 25 = 169 = 13².

q.t: Two vertical poles 6 m and 11 m high stand 12 m apart on level ground. Find the distance between their tops (in m).
q.e: The tops differ in height by 5 m and are 12 m apart sideways. Right triangle: 25 + 144 = 169 = 13².

q.t: In △ABC, ∠A is 20° more than ∠B, and ∠C is 20° less than ∠B. Find ∠A (in degrees).
The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm and 30 cm. Find the length of each side (in cm).
q.e: The diagonals cut each other in half at right angles, making right triangles with legs 8 and 15: 64 + 225 = 289 = 17².

q.t: The three exterior angles of a triangle (one at each vertex) add up to:
q.e: Each exterior + interior pair is 180°, so three pairs total 540°. Remove the interior sum of 180°: 360°.

q.t: In △ABC, ∠A = 70°. The bisectors of ∠B and ∠C meet at O. Find ∠BOC (in degrees).
q.e: ∠B + ∠C = 110°, so their halves add to 55°. In △BOC the third angle is 180 − 55 = 125°.

q.t: A tree breaks 5 m above the ground and its top touches the ground 12 m from the base. How tall was the tree (in m)?
q.e: The broken part is the hypotenuse: 25 + 144 = 169 → 13 m. Total height = 5 + 13 = 18 m.

q.t: Two sides of a triangle are 4 cm and 9 cm. How many whole-number lengths (in cm) are possible for the third side?
q.k: len([c for c in range(1,30) if 9-4<c<9+4])
q.e: The third side must be more than 9 − 4 = 5 and less than 9 + 4 = 13: so 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 or 12 — seven values.

q.t: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm, and its legs differ by 7 cm. Find the shorter leg (in cm).
q.k: [x for x in range(1,13) if x*x+(x+7)**2==169][0]
q.e: Legs x and x + 7 with x² + (x + 7)² = 169. Try x = 5: 25 + 144 = 169 ✓.

q.t: An exterior angle of a triangle is 105° and the two interior opposite angles are equal. Find each (in degrees).
q.e: They add up to the exterior angle, so each is 105 ÷ 2 = 52.5.

q.t: In △ABC, AB = AC and ∠A = 2 × ∠B. Find ∠A (in degrees).
q.e: AB = AC makes ∠B = ∠C. So 2B + B + B = 180, B = 45 and ∠A = 90.
